name: Just the start
why: 5: the van collects at its own junction.

name: No way back
why: 4: the street is one-way, so from 1 the van cannot reach 0.

name: A loop
why: 6: the van goes round and collects every junction once.

name: Into a loop and out again
why: 12: go to 1, come back to 0, then go to 2. A search that never visits a junction twice finds only 7.

name: Choose the better branch
why: 16: 0 → 1 → 3. The two branches cannot both be taken.

name: Each junction counts once
why: 9. Going round a loop again collects nothing more. A rule that adds values along a walk never stops here.

name: Out of reach
why: 2: junctions 2 and 3 lead to 0, but 0 cannot reach them.

name: Repeated streets and a street to itself
Greedy goes wrong
why: 12: the long way 0 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 beats the single 9. Picking the richest next junction fails.

name: Two loops joined
why: 52: from the first loop, the street to 5 is worth more than the second loop (6). Each loop is one group, worth its total.

name: A loop with two exits
why: 10: starting inside the loop, collect it all (3), then leave by the better exit, 4 (7).

name: A tangle of 30
why: Trying every walk, or every set of visited junctions, is far too slow even here. Group the loops first.

name: A one-way chain of 100,000
show: streets k → k + 1 for k up to 99,998, every value 1
why: 100,000. The search is 100,000 levels deep: a recursive search stops at about 1,000.

name: A ring of 100,000
show: a one-way ring of 100,000 junctions with random values
why: One group holds every junction, so the answer is the sum of all values. A recursive group search fails; so does any rule that walks the ring again and again.

name: A chain of 30,000 loops
show: 30,000 loops of three junctions, each leading on to the next loop and to the one after it
why: Each loop is one group and the groups form a long DAG. Collapse the loops, then one pass over the groups in topological order.

name: 60,000 junctions, random
why: One big group and many small ones. Group search, then the DAG pass: O(V + E).
